A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLBFF work and contain 19 readable pages, including Appendices A–D. Pages 2–19 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; the differences are confined to page 1.

before.justification: v1 reports original human verification of principle extraction, reward-model evaluations and ablations in Tables 2–4, and model-alignment experiments in Table 5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original human-verification results, reward-model experiments, ablations, and model-alignment outcomes reported in v1.

M1.justification: Principle extraction and filtering, scalar and generative reward modeling, and GRPO alignment are identical in Sections 3–6 and Appendices A–B.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HelpSteer3 training data and evaluate on RM-Bench, JudgeBench, PrincipleBench, MT-Bench, WildBench, and Arena Hard v2. Domain, language, and task coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 2–5, including Bradley-Terry, Nemotron, RewardAnything, RM-R1, R3, fixed-principle variants, and the alignment baselines.

E3.justification: Sample selection, model configurations, training budgets, evaluation principles, metrics, and judging procedures are unchanged throughout Sections 3–6 and Appendices A–D.

E4.justification: Both retain the same consensus-threshold and fixed-principle ablations, response-order analysis, human verification, and Appendix D investigation of style-controlled score reproducibility.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains the same 95% confidence-interval reporting, and Section 3 retains the same annotation-agreement statistics. No repeated-run, seed, or statistical-testing information is added or removed.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including appendix findings. Table 2 still reports 86.2 on RM-Bench and 81.4 on JudgeBench for Flexible Principles GenRM; Table 3 retains 91.6 overall for Flexible Principles ScalarRM.

T1.justification: The principle definition, reward-scoring formulation, and Appendix C averaging calculation are unchanged. No assumptions, mathematical reasoning, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain identical scientific claims about RLBFF, PrincipleBench, reward-model performance, and economical Qwen3-32B alignment. The added model link does not revise these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of filtering tradeoffs, position bias, GenRM weaknesses on PrincipleBench, and judge/style-control limitations remain identical in the main text and Appendix D.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Models link below the abstract pointing to NVIDIA’s Hugging Face reward-model collection. This supplies new model-access information; implementation details remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not verify the linked collection’s contents.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations, bibliography, and positioning relative to prior reward-modeling research are identical. The model-collection link adds no related-work comparison.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short Models line and updates the first-page arXiv version/date stamp. Existing prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added model-link line and Hugging Face icon slightly adjust first-page spacing and Table 1 placement. Scientific figure and table designs are retained, and pages 2–19 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The new first-page model-collection link modestly improves artifact discoverability and access documentation. Scientific content, empirical support, and Appendices A–D remain unchanged, so the benefit is limited; it does not establish that additional artifacts were released.
